key_insight: DiffHDR leverages conditional video diffusion models to re-expose 8-bit LDR videos, hallucinating plausible highlight and shadow detail lost to saturation/quantization while preserving temporal consistency and enabling controllable exposure adjustments.
problem_solved: Converting ubiquitous 8-bit LDR videos into usable HDR for re-exposure and display—recovering realistic detail in clipped highlights and deep shadows and avoiding per-frame temporal artifacts that prior LDR→HDR expansion methods produce.
method: Train a conditional video diffusion model that maps LDR frames (plus optional target exposure) to HDR outputs.
Design spatio-temporal conditioning (video-aware U-Net / temporal attention) to enforce frame-to-frame consistency and reduce flicker.
Use exposure-aware conditioning and perceptual/temporal objectives to hallucinate plausible detail in saturated regions and support interactive re-exposure control.
impact: Provides a practical route to restore and re-expose archived or consumer LDR video for HDR displays and post-production workflows, improving visual quality and enabling downstream vision tasks that benefit from expanded dynamic range.
visual_elements: Before/after slider comparing original LDR frame vs DiffHDR-restored HDR frame (showing recovered highlights/shadows).
Small UI mockup with an exposure/re-exposure slider controlling output brightness and tone mapping.
Block diagram of the video diffusion pipeline showing LDR input, temporal conditioning, diffusion denoising steps, and HDR output.
Temporal stability visualization (frame difference heatmap or flicker chart) comparing per-frame LDR→HDR baselines vs DiffHDR.
paper_title: DiffHDR: Re-Exposing LDR Videos with Video Diffusion Models
paper_authors: Zhengming Yu, Li Ma, Mingming He, Leo Isikdogan, Yuancheng Xu
